How do you get from Phoenix Airport (PHX) to Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters runs private transfers between Phoenix Sky Harbor and Scottsdale, which sits 12 to 25 miles northeast of the airport depending on which part of town you are going to — the shortest of those runs is Old Town Scottsdale, 12 miles out. Four ways make the trip: rideshare, priced by the app at the moment you request it; a shared airport shuttle, cheaper per seat but stopping for other passengers first; a metered taxi from the posted terminal ranks; and a private chauffeured transfer, reserved before you fly, with the flight tracked and the vehicle sized to the group. Our published transfer runs from $225 one way in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) to $295 in the Executive Black Sprinter, before 8% Arizona sales tax.

Last updated: September 20, 2026

How far is Phoenix Airport from Scottsdale?

Scottsdale is roughly 12 to 25 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor, and which end of that range applies depends entirely on the address: Old Town Scottsdale (85251) is about 12 miles from the terminals, while North Scottsdale — Troon North and DC Ranch sits about 25 miles out at the city's far northeastern edge. Between those two, Paradise Valley (85253) is about 14 miles from the terminals, and North Scottsdale and Kierland (85254) is about 18 miles from the terminals. This guide publishes the miles and no drive time, because the same 12-mile Old Town Scottsdale run behaves differently at 7am on a Monday, at 5pm on a Friday and at midnight, and the farther areas move further still. Give the reservations team a full street address rather than a resort's marketing name: similar names sit in different ZIP codes, and a gated community adds a checkpoint no map shows.

What is a car service to and from Sky Harbor?

A car service between Phoenix Sky Harbor and Scottsdale is a chauffeured vehicle reserved before you fly, assigned to your party and priced as a trip between two addresses — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, and priced from the drive beyond that, with the empty return included — rather than by a meter or by an app at the moment you request it. A Sky Harbor car service booking carries your professional chauffeur, the vehicle you selected, flight tracking on airport work and bottled water on board; a car service from Phoenix airport to a Scottsdale address is $225 one way in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and $295 in the Executive Black Sprinter, before 8% Arizona sales tax. The 9 vehicles this page carries run smallest first, from 6 seats in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) at $125 an hour to 56 in the 56-Passenger Motorcoach at $325. Hourly work never bills below the vehicle's own minimum: 4 hours on 8 of the 9, and 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A 4-hour block therefore starts at $500 on the Luxury SUV (Suburban), about $83 a seat, and the lowest per-seat split on the page is the 56-Passenger Motorcoach at $29 a seat. Every rate, minimum, 4-hour total and per-seat figure is in the grid below. Curbside pickup and meet-and-greet are different methods and the confirmation states which one you booked. An optional greeter meets the party at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with bags for $200 flat. A Scottsdale Airport arrival sits on the same reservation — the airport service is listed as Phoenix Sky Harbor & SDL Transportation — so a Scottsdale Airport (SCF/SDL) trip is quoted from the vehicles and figures above rather than a separate price list. Put the outbound leg on the same booking and the 20% return credit applies, so the car service to Sky Harbor is quoted from the same table as the run into town; it is the same airport car service Scottsdale residents book for a departure and visitors book for an arrival.

Which vehicle fits the group and its bags?

Count people and cargo as 2 separate inventories, then take the smallest vehicle that clears both: 6 seats in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) for a solo traveller, a couple or a small family, 8 to 14 across the Maybach and executive Sprinters, and 24 to 56 across the mini buses and the coach. A family with checked cases usually wants the next size up rather than the last free seat: the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter seats 8 and the Maybach Jet Sprinter seats 9, both with a taller cabin and an upright step. Six to fourteen people fit the Executive Black Sprinter or Executive White Sprinter at 14 seats each; from fifteen to fifty-six the range runs Mini Bus (24 Pax), Executive Mini Bus — Grech (27 Pax), Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) and the 56-Passenger Motorcoach, which carries 56 with under-floor bays. Seated capacity is a planning ceiling, not a luggage promise, so describe the bags.

What happens at the terminal — curbside, or meet-and-greet?

Phoenix Sky Harbor organises ground transportation around its 2 active terminals, Terminal 3 and Terminal 4, and a prearranged vehicle follows its own permitted commercial instruction rather than the public taxi positions, so stay inside until the chauffeur confirms the vehicle is approaching the assigned location. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit. The airport's published taxi references are Terminal 3's north curb outside Door 7, and Terminal 4's Level 1 curbs outside north Door 7 and south Door 4 — landmarks, not a promise that a chauffeured vehicle loads there. Curbside pickup and meet-and-greet are different methods and the confirmation states which one you booked. Flight tracking is included on airport work, so a delay moves the pickup instead of costing the booking — but it cannot see a slow belt, so the trip lead confirms when everyone is curb-ready. An optional greeter meets the party at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with bags for $200 flat.

Rideshare, shared shuttle, taxi, or a private chauffeured transfer?

The honest split is by party size, bags and certainty: 1 or 2 people travelling light have four workable options, a family with checked cases has three, and a group of six or more with luggage is usually down to one vehicle reserved in advance and sized to the manifest. Rideshare and shared shuttles both operate at Phoenix Sky Harbor and price their own way — rideshare by the app when you request it, shuttles by their own tariffs — so we do not quote their fares. A rideshare fare moves with time of day and demand; a shared shuttle is cheaper per seat but collects other passengers first; a metered taxi loads from the posted ranks. A private transfer trades that flexibility for certainty: the vehicle is assigned before you fly, the price is the figure you agreed, and one vehicle moves the whole party and its bags rather than splitting nine people across three cars.

What does a private transfer from PHX to Scottsdale cost?

There are 2 published ways to price the same ride: a point-to-point transfer, where the Luxury SUV (Suburban) is $225 one way and the Executive Black Sprinter is $295, or an hourly charter at the published rate against the vehicle's own minimum, which is $500 and $580 respectively before tax. Take the transfer price when the trip is airport to address. One-way figures run from $225 on the Luxury SUV (Suburban) to $1,250 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach; the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter is $395 and the Maybach Jet Sprinter is $550. Book both legs together and a 20% credit applies to the return leg — $236 rather than $295 on the Executive Black Sprinter. An added stop on a transfer leg is $50. Take the hourly rate when the vehicle should wait or collect a second flight: rate times billable hours, never below the 4-hour minimum, or 5 on the 56-Passenger Motorcoach. A 4-hour block is $780 on the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and $740 on the Mini Bus (24 Pax). The table above carries the current published hourly rates; check availability and request a current quote for your date, vehicle and trip details.

What is included, and what is added at checkout?

Included in every published figure: your professional chauffeur, the assigned vehicle, flight tracking on airport work and bottled water on board. Added at checkout: Arizona sales tax of 8%, the 50% deposit, and what you choose yourself — there is no booking fee, service charge or fuel surcharge on the base fare. The optional extras an arrival asks about are the greeter at $200 flat, a child seat fitted before pickup, and a named welcome sign. None are added for you, and gratuity is optional. A transfer price covers the ride between the two addresses you gave; stops sit inside an hourly charter, where you hold the whole vehicle.

How do booking, changes and cancellation work?

A 50% deposit confirms the reservation and the balance is charged to the card on file 48 hours before pickup, with Arizona sales tax of 8% added at checkout; cancellation terms are tiered by trip type and quoted in full below. Cancel 14 or more days before pickup and you get a full refund. Between 72 hours and 14 days we keep the deposit and refund the rest; inside 72 hours the reservation is non-refundable. Large groups, party buses and weddings (20+ passengers or two or more vehicles) get a full refund 30 or more days out and keep-the-deposit terms down to 14 days. Major-event dates — Barrett-Jackson Scottsdale, WM Phoenix Open, Cactus League spring training weekend, New Year's Eve, Prom weekend — run on a longer window of 60 days, and the deposit there is non-refundable: cancel 60 or more days ahead and the balance is refunded; inside 60 days nothing is refunded. If we ever cancel on our side, you get 100% back. Send the airline and flight number exactly as booked, the passenger and bag counts, the Scottsdale address and a day-of mobile contact. Reach the reservations team on (623) 986-6339 or at reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com.

Can the same vehicle carry on to Sedona or elsewhere in Arizona?

Yes, and the 2 onward runs asked for most are Sedona and the Grand Canyon — both booked as their own private transfer or hourly day rather than improvised at the curb, because a long run carries its own vehicle, route and timing decisions. A Phoenix or Scottsdale to Sedona run has its own service page and its own quote, covered by the same executive Sprinters and coaches listed here. Describe the whole shape of the trip when you first ask: an arrival, local movement and a Sedona day quoted together beat three unrelated bookings.

Frequently asked questions

How far is Phoenix airport to Scottsdale?

About 12 to 25 miles, depending on where in Scottsdale you are going: Old Town Scottsdale about 12 miles; Paradise Valley about 14 miles; North Scottsdale and Kierland about 18 miles; North Scottsdale — Troon North and DC Ranch about 25 miles. Give the full street address.

How long does the drive from PHX to Scottsdale take?

This guide publishes no drive time, only the distance: Old Town Scottsdale is 12 miles out and North Scottsdale — Troon North and DC Ranch about 25, and the same drive behaves differently at rush hour and at midnight. The transfer price does not change with traffic.

How much is an Uber from Phoenix airport to Scottsdale?

We do not publish rideshare fares and cannot quote them: that price is set by the app when you request the ride and moves with time of day and demand. Our own published figure for the same trip is $225 one way in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), before 8% tax.

How much is a car service from Sky Harbor to Scottsdale?

A one-way transfer is $225 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban), $395 in the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter and $295 in the Executive Black Sprinter, before 8% Arizona sales tax. Priced hourly instead, the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and the Executive Black Sprinter are $125 and $145 an hour against a 4-hour minimum — $500 and $580 for the block. The rate grid on this page carries the same figures for every vehicle.

How do you get from Phoenix airport to Scottsdale?

Four ways: rideshare, a shared airport shuttle, a metered taxi from the posted terminal ranks, or a private chauffeured transfer reserved in advance. The first three are decided at the airport on the day; a private transfer is assigned before you fly and tracks the flight.

Is a car service better than a shuttle from PHX?

It depends on the party. A shared airport shuttle is cheaper per seat but collects other passengers first; a private car service is assigned before you fly, the price is the figure you agreed, and one vehicle moves the whole party and its bags rather than splitting the group across several cars. We do not publish shuttle fares and cannot quote them, so the comparison to make is party size, bags and certainty rather than a price we have no source for.

Which terminal will my chauffeur meet me at?

Terminal 3 or Terminal 4, whichever your flight arrives at, but at the permitted commercial location for that terminal, which can differ from the public taxi curb. Scottsdale Sprinters holds the Phoenix Sky Harbor (PHX) ground transportation permit. Stay inside until the chauffeur confirms the vehicle is close.

Do you track my flight?

Yes, on airport work: a delay moves the pickup rather than costing you the booking. Tracking cannot see a slow baggage belt, so your trip lead should still message when everyone and every bag is ready at the curb.

Is a greeter included, or is it extra?

Optional and extra. A greeter meets the party at baggage claim with a name sign and helps with the bags; it is $200 flat on an airport arrival, and appears on the quote only if you select it. Curbside pickup with no greeter is the default.

What vehicle do we need for a group of twelve with luggage?

The Executive Black Sprinter or Executive White Sprinter, 14 seats each at $145 per hour on a 4-hour minimum, or $295 as a one-way transfer. Twelve seats and twelve large cases are different questions, so describe the bags.

What does a round trip cost?

Book both legs together and a 20% credit applies to the return leg: on the Executive Black Sprinter that makes the return $236 rather than $295. The credit is offered only when both legs are reserved together.

How do I book an airport transfer?

Check live rates and availability on the pricing page, call or text (623) 986-6339, or email reservations@scottsdalesprinters.com with the flight number, passenger and bag counts and the Scottsdale address. A 50% deposit confirms the reservation.
